title: Tumor-area mitosis proportion as an image-derived mitotic phenotype in lung squamous cell carcinoma: Patient-level prognostic and multi-omics evaluation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Tumor-area mitosis proportion as an image-derived mitotic phenotype in lung squamous cell carcinoma: Patient-level prognostic and multi-omics evaluation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0040】The study addressed four related objectives. First, we adapted a transfer-learning-based mitosis classifier from MIDOG to LUSC WSI patches. Second, we derived TAMP as a patient-level measure of the prevalence of mitosis-positive regions within pathologist-defined tumor tissue. Third, we evaluated whether TAMP was associated with overall survival and whether this relationship persisted after adjustment for available clinical prognostic factors, while also examining its associations with selected immune and genomic characteristics. Fourth, we integrated TAMP with transcriptomic pathway enrichment, predicted drug-response analysis, and inferred transcription-factor activity to characterize the molecular context of tumors with elevated mitosis-associated morphology. This framework extends automated mitosis analysis from local image classification toward patient-level clinicopathological and multi-omics characterization.

【Introduction · p0010】Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide and continues to impose a substantial clinical burden.1, 2 Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), a major histological subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, accounts for approximately 25%–30% of lung cancer cases and typically originates from the bronchial epithelium of the central airways.3, 4 LUSC is strongly associated with tobacco exposure and is characterized by recurrent genomic alterations involving TP53, CDKN2A, PIK3CA, and other genes governing cell-cycle regulation and tumor growth.5 Unlike lung adenocarcinoma, however, LUSC has relatively few routinely actionable molecular alterations, limiting opportunities for genotype-directed treatment, and reinforcing the need for additional markers that can better characterize tumor aggressiveness and support prognostic assessment.6

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Tumor-area mitosis proportion as an image-derived mitotic phenotype in lung squamous cell carcinoma: Patient-level prognostic and multi-omics evaluation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Data acquisition and cohort selection · p0105】The source-domain subset used in this study consisted exclusively of 150 H&E-stained WSIs of invasive breast carcinoma from MIDOG 2022. No non-breast tissue domains from the broader MIDOG resources were included in source-domain model development. The slides were acquired at 40× magnification with a nominal spatial resolution of 0.25 μm/pixel, and expert-annotated mitotic figures provided the reference labels for training. This subset was selected because it combines standardized expert annotation with substantial scanner- and stain-related variability, providing an appropriate source domain for cross-tissue adaptation to LUSC.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】The analysis combined MIDOG 2022 with TCGA-LUSC, including 478 patients and 512 diagnostic WSIs after quality control. Tumor regions and mitotic figures were reviewed by two pathologists with interobserver agreement of Cohen's κ ≥ 0.85. A ResNet-50 model was trained on MIDOG and subsequently adapted to TCGA-LUSC using Focal Loss and stain-aware augmentation. Target-domain performance was evaluated using patient-level stratified 5-fold cross-validation and an additional WSI-level holdout analysis to address potential leakage from the initial patch-level partitioning. TAMP was calculated from patient-level out-of-fold predictions as the proportion of evaluable tumor patches classified as mitosis-positive. Associations with overall survival, immune and genomic features, transcriptomic programs, predicted drug response, and transcription-factor activity were subsequently examined. Multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, tumor stage, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Tumor-area mitosis proportion as an image-derived mitotic phenotype in lung squamous cell carcinoma: Patient-level prognostic and multi-omics evaluation》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · f0005】Fig. 1 ResNet-50 model performance and interpretability on the internal MIDOG test set (n=2,000 image patches). (A) Receiver operating characteristic curve for patch-level mitosis classification, yielding an AUC of 0.975 (95% CI: 0.965–0.980). (B) Confusion matrix at the Youden-optimal operating threshold, showing 811 true positives, 10 false negatives, 189 false positives, and 990 true negatives. (C) Representative Grad-CAM heatmaps showing that model activation is concentrated on mitotic figures.

【Fig. 2 · f0010】Fig. 2 Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and Cox regression for patient-level out-of-fold TAMP estimates. Kaplan–Meier curves are stratified by high versus low TAMP groups, showing significantly poorer overall survival (OS) in the high-TAMP group (log-rank p=0.008). Univariable Cox regression yielded a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.82 (95% CI: 1.18–2.81), corresponding to an 82% higher hazard of death in the high-TAMP group. In multivariable analysis adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, tumor stage, and ECOG performance status, high TAMP remained significantly associated with poorer OS (adjusted HR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.08–2.62; p=0.022).

【Fig. 3 · f0015】Fig. 3 Associations between tumor-area mitosis proportion (TAMP) and selected components of the tumor microenvironment in the TCGA-LUSC cohort. TAMP was negatively correlated with stromal fraction r′=−0.117p=0.041 and resting memory CD4+T cells r′=−0.158p=0.010, whereas activated mast cells r′=0.129p=0.034 and M1 macrophages r′=0.105p=0.025 showed modest positive correlations. Overall leukocyte fraction, CD8+ T cells, and regulatory T cells were not significantly associated with TAMP.

【Data availability · p0005】The TCGA-LUSC diagnostic WSIs and matched clinical, genomic, and transcriptomic data analyzed in this study are publicly available through the National Cancer Institute Genomic Data Commons. The MIDOG 2022 dataset used for source-domain model development is available through the MIDOG 2022 challenge platform under the applicable data-use conditions. Derived study materials, including TCGA-LUSC annotation masks, patch coordinates, patient-level out-of-fold TAMP estimates, trained model weights, and the inference pipeline, are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request for non-commercial research purposes, subject to applicable institutional and source-data use policies.

【Statistical and survival analysis · p0280】All statistical analyses were performed in R version 4.3.0. Associations between continuous TAMP values and clinicopathological or molecular variables were evaluated using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. Comparisons between two independent groups were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test, whereas variables with three or more categories were evaluated using the Kruskal–Wallis test.
